top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is a measurement-driven advance with independent confirmation: several laboratories compare lattice clocks and agree at the 1e-18 level. It has a compact two-name attribution and lasting reach into gravitational redshift tests, varying constants and dark-matter searches. The lineage with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a real caveat, but the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct regime. P002 (twisted bilayer graphene) is strong physics, but its maturity, credit (Cao and earlier moire band-structure theory left out) and the unresolved pairing mechanism make it second. A prize is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the slate has no PAMELA, Fermi-LAT or polarimetry work, and these are outside my own expertise in atomic and condensed-matter topics
